Team —

We need a concise package for the executive QBR (April 6). The ask is 3 things:

1) One-slide operational summary (to include current GPU spend, utilization, and run-rate runway impact).
2) One-slide unit-economics snapshot showing per-100k-token cost today vs. target after planned batching/caching/quantization changes.
3) A short mitigation playbook (canary/fallback routing + quota uplift plan) if demand spikes during next quarter.

Please include hard numbers and one-sentence confidence levels. I want the slides by COB Wed (3/31) so I can combine for the exec pack.

Data hints for the slide deck:
- Q1 GPU spend (public clouds + Dedicated) and committed vs. variable split
- Avg GPU utilization by pool and P95 tail utilization
- Measured per-token cost (generation) + embedding unit costs
- Measured savings from prefix/KV caching and continuous batching experiments (actual and simulated)
- Expected delta from proposed quantization on the 30B family (if you have sims)

Marissa — can you own the spend/runway numbers? Vivek — can you pull utilization, batching/caching sims, and the risk-mitigation bullets? Markus — I need a one-line ask for finance (discounts/commitments) and an idea for incremental reserved capacity to buy down unit cost.

Attach anything you want me to forward to Sarah (Acme) — she asked for a short note on cost impact for their pilot.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan / Marissa —

I pulled utilization and ran the batching/cache sims; attaching the PDF with the matrices. Highlights:

- Pool-level utilization (weighted avg across shared + dedicated): 58% avg GPU utilization; P95 usage at 82% (spikes tied to 18:00–21:00 UTC retail windows).
- Observed: continuous batching increased tokens/sec by 1.9x on our 8xA100 pools for typical short-chat workloads; average per-token compute latency reduced ~22% (measured).
- Caching: prefix/KV caching reduced repeating-token generation by ~12% in pilot customers (notably in the Acme pilot). Combined batching + caching reduces per-token compute cost by ~28% in our sim (mix-sensitive).
- Quantization: early sim (static) on 30B family shows potential extra 15% CPU/GPU ops reduction but with a 2–4% accuracy delta on our eval set — need product sign-off on tolerance.

Risk / mitigation bullets (short):
- If demand spikes >20% above current peaks, tail latency will hit >P95 350ms on shared pools.
  - Mitigation: auto-burst to dedicated pool variant + failover to lower-cost quantized model family for non-SLA routes.
- Canary plan: route 5% traffic to quantized variant for 48 hours and monitor eval prompts; gate: <3% regression.

I'll drop the sims PDF and a 1-slide summary into the Drive link. Let me know if you want a short table linking cost delta to predicted ARR impact for Acme.

Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: batching_cache_simulations.pdf
